title: NVIDIA launched GeForce GTX 1060 3GB 10 years ago, but it wasn’t the last 3GB GeForce
article:
NVIDIA’s GeForce GTX 1060 3GB turns 10
Ten years ago, NVIDIA launched the GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, a cheaper version of its Pascal-based GTX 1060. The card arrived on August 18, 2016, about one month after the original GTX 1060 6GB, with an MSRP of $199 compared with $249 for the 6GB model.
Despite sharing the same GTX 1060 name, the 3GB card did not simply have half the memory. NVIDIA also disabled one of the ten Streaming Multiprocessors on the GP106 GPU. This reduced the CUDA core count from 1,280 to 1,152 and the number of texture units from 80 to 72.
Both versions retained a 192-bit GDDR5 memory interface with memory running at 8 Gbps, providing 192 GB/s of bandwidth. The reference GPU clocks were also unchanged at 1506 MHz base and 1708 MHz boost, while the board power remained at 120W. The reduced GPU configuration meant the 3GB version was slower even in workloads that did not exceed its smaller framebuffer.
NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 Specifications
NVIDIA introduced covered the GTX 1060 3GB on August 18, 2016. At the time, NVIDIA had originally planned to launch the card on August 24, but the release was moved forward. Board partners quickly followed with custom models based on the 1,152-core configuration.
The GTX 1060 3GB was not NVIDIA’s final desktop GeForce with 3GB of memory. In May 2018, NVIDIA introduced the GeForce GTX 1050 3GB. That model used the full 768-core GP107 configuration but paired it with a narrower 96-bit memory bus.
Did any of you own a GTX 1060 3GB? I still have mine, although it’s broken now.
